facts.f: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean.
facts.e: It is bigger than all of Earth's land put together.

facts.f: Earth has five oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic.
facts.e: They are all connected, making one big world ocean.

facts.f: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest ocean.
facts.e: Much of it is covered by sea ice for most of the year.

facts.f: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific is the deepest known part of the ocean.
facts.e: Its deepest point is nearly 11 km below the surface.

facts.f: If Mount Everest were dropped into the Mariana Trench, its top would still be underwater.
facts.e: The trench is about 2 km deeper than Everest is tall.

facts.f: The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country.
facts.e: It is the third-largest ocean and touches India's southern coasts.

facts.f: Seawater is salty mainly because of salts washed off the land.
facts.e: Over millions of years, rain and rivers carried tiny bits of salt from rocks into the sea.

facts.f: On average, seawater is about 3.5% salt.
facts.e: That means about 35 grams of salt in every litre of seawater.

facts.f: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived.
facts.e: It is heavier than any dinosaur and can grow to about 30 metres long.

facts.f: Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called coral polyps.
facts.e: Polyps build hard skeletons of limestone that pile up over thousands of years.

facts.f: The Great Barrier Reef off Australia is the largest coral reef system in the world.
facts.e: It is so big that it can be seen from space.

facts.f: Corals can turn white when the water gets too warm. This is called coral bleaching.
facts.e: Stressed corals push out the tiny algae that live in them and give them colour and food.

facts.f: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.
facts.e: Its blood uses copper, not iron, to carry oxygen, which makes it blue.

facts.f: A shark's skeleton is made of cartilage, not bone.
facts.e: Cartilage is the bendy material in your ears and nose.

facts.f: A starfish is not a fish.
facts.e: Sea stars belong to a group called echinoderms. Many can regrow a lost arm.

facts.f: A jellyfish has no brain, no heart and no bones.
facts.e: It uses a simple net of nerves to sense its surroundings.

facts.f: Seahorse fathers carry the eggs and give birth to the babies.
facts.e: The mother puts her eggs into a pouch on the father's belly.

facts.f: Dolphins and whales are mammals, not fish.
facts.e: They breathe air through a blowhole and feed their babies milk.

facts.f: The deep ocean is completely dark.
facts.e: Sunlight cannot reach below about 1,000 metres.

facts.f: Many deep-sea creatures make their own light.
facts.e: This is called bioluminescence. They use it to find food, hide or attract mates.

facts.f: Tiny plant-like living things called phytoplankton make a large part of Earth's oxygen.
facts.e: Scientists estimate that about half of the oxygen made on Earth each year comes from the ocean.

facts.f: The Gulf Stream is a warm ocean current in the Atlantic.
facts.e: It carries warm water from the Gulf of Mexico towards Europe, helping keep western Europe milder.

facts.f: In most places the tide rises and falls about twice a day.
facts.e: These are high tide and low tide.

facts.f: Olive ridley sea turtles nest in huge numbers on Odisha's beaches, such as Gahirmatha.
facts.e: Thousands of females come ashore together to lay their eggs. This is called an arribada.

facts.f: Water pressure grows as you go deeper in the ocean.
facts.e: At the bottom of the Mariana Trench the pressure is more than 1,000 times that at the surface.

facts.f: Seawater freezes at a lower temperature than fresh water.
facts.e: Because of the salt, seawater freezes at about minus 2 degrees Celsius instead of 0.

facts.f: The Bay of Bengal is the largest bay in the world.
facts.e: It lies to the east of India.

facts.f: Lakshadweep is made of coral islands in the Arabian Sea.
facts.e: Many of its islands are atolls: rings of coral around a lagoon.

facts.f: The Sundarbans, in India and Bangladesh, is the largest mangrove forest in the world.
facts.e: Mangroves are trees that grow in salty water along coasts.

facts.f: Pearls are made by oysters and some other shellfish.
facts.e: When something irritating gets inside the shell, the oyster coats it with smooth layers until a pearl forms.

facts.f: The whale shark is the largest fish in the world.
facts.e: Even though it is huge, it eats tiny plankton and small fish.

facts.f: Fish breathe with gills.
facts.e: Gills take in oxygen that is dissolved in the water.

facts.f: Clownfish live safely among the stinging tentacles of sea anemones.
facts.e: A special slime on the clownfish's skin protects it from stings.

facts.f: Most volcanic activity on Earth happens under the sea.
facts.e: Lava erupts along long cracks in the ocean floor called mid-ocean ridges.

facts.f: The longest mountain range on Earth is mostly underwater.
facts.e: The mid-ocean ridge winds through the oceans for about 65,000 km.

facts.f: Almost all penguins live in the Southern Hemisphere.
facts.e: No penguins live in the wild near the North Pole.

facts.f: An octopus can change its colour and skin texture in a flash.
facts.e: It does this to hide from predators or sneak up on prey.

facts.f: The Dead Sea is so salty that people float easily in it.
facts.e: It is actually a salt lake, not a sea.

facts.f: The ocean takes in about a quarter of the carbon dioxide that people release.
facts.e: This slows global warming, but it is also making seawater more acidic.

facts.f: Most ocean waves are made by the wind.
facts.e: Wind blowing across the water pushes it into ripples and then waves.

facts.f: Sea turtles often return to the beach where they hatched to lay their own eggs.
facts.e: Scientists think they use Earth's magnetic field to find their way back.

facts.f: Sea otters sometimes hold paws while they sleep.
facts.e: This keeps them from drifting apart on the water.

quiz.q: Which is the largest ocean?
quiz.x: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean.

quiz.q: What is the deepest known place in the ocean?
quiz.x: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific is nearly 11 km deep.

quiz.q: Which is the only ocean named after a country?
quiz.x: The Indian Ocean is named after India.

quiz.q: Which is the smallest ocean?
quiz.x: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest.

quiz.q: What builds coral reefs?
quiz.x: Coral polyps build limestone skeletons that form reefs.

quiz.q: In seahorses, who carries the babies?
quiz.x: Seahorse fathers carry the eggs in a pouch and give birth.

quiz.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
quiz.x: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.

quiz.q: Which is the largest fish?
quiz.x: The blue whale is bigger, but it is a mammal, not a fish.

quiz.q: What is a shark's skeleton made of?
quiz.x: Sharks have skeletons of cartilage, the bendy material in your ears.

quiz.q: What do fish breathe with?
quiz.x: Gills take oxygen from the water.

quiz.q: What kind of animal is a dolphin?
quiz.x: Dolphins breathe air and feed their babies milk, like other mammals.

quiz.q: Which is the largest mangrove forest in the world?
quiz.x: The Sundarbans spreads across India and Bangladesh.

quiz.q: Which is the largest coral reef system in the world?
quiz.x: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of Australia.

quiz.q: Which tiny plant-like ocean living things make a lot of Earth's oxygen?
quiz.x: Phytoplankton use sunlight to make food and release oxygen.

quiz.q: What is it called when living things make their own light?
quiz.x: Many deep-sea creatures, and fireflies on land, are bioluminescent.

quiz.q: Gahirmatha beach in Odisha is famous for which animal?
quiz.x: Huge numbers of olive ridley turtles come ashore there to lay eggs.

quiz.q: What makes most ocean waves?
quiz.x: Wind blowing over the sea pushes the water into waves. Tides are different and come mainly from the Moon.

quiz.q: Why is seawater salty?
o: Salts were washed from land rocks by rivers
quiz.x: Over millions of years rivers carried dissolved salts into the oceans.

quiz.q: The Dead Sea is actually a...
quiz.x: The Dead Sea is a very salty lake between Jordan and Israel.

quiz.q: What is a starfish?
quiz.x: Sea stars belong to the echinoderm family, along with sea urchins.

quiz.q: Where do almost all penguins live?
quiz.x: Penguins live in Antarctica and southern coasts, not in the Arctic.
